blocks.text: BRUSSELS, Belgium — Artificial intelligence could help Nato forces’ weapons systems communicate more effectively with one another, a top commander in the alliance said Wednesday. Having already transformed the way wars are fought on the ground, AI can also help forces process vast amounts of information and improve “interoperability,” said Nato Supreme Allied Commander Transformation French Adm. Pierre Vandier. “For Nato, it’s extraordinary news because now we run AI interoperability,” he told reporters at Nato headquarters in Brussels. This could improve the compatibility of different allied combat systems, allowing them to share information beyond their existing standards. READ: 1997: Russia wants […]...
